nodes.name: Webhook: Approval Request
nodes.notes: POST {action_id, action_type, requested_by, summary, details?, amount?, timeout_minutes?}. Replies at once with "pending"; the wait for a human happens after the reply.

nodes.name: Webhook: Approval Response
nodes.notes: Slack interaction (button click) OR direct API call {action_id, decision, responder}. rawBody is on so the Slack signature can be verified against the exact bytes Slack signed.

nodes.name: CONFIG
nodes.notes: THE ONLY NODE YOU NEED TO EDIT. Service URLs, secrets, who may approve, timeout limits. See the Read Me First note and the README.

nodes.name: Approval Policy
nodes.notes: EDIT ME for who-approves-what and wording: which action types are accepted, per-type approvers, timeouts, self-approval ban and the details shown in Slack, plus the messages requesters get. Data only; checked on every request. It can only make approvals stricter than CONFIG.

nodes.name: Is Response Flow?
nodes.notes: Both webhooks share one CONFIG node; this sends each request down its own flow.

nodes.name: Validate Request
nodes.notes: Checks the caller (optional token), CONFIG and the request. Bad input is rejected with 400 and a specific message; nothing is silently changed (the original quietly turned an invalid timeout into 60 minutes).

nodes.name: Create Approval
nodes.notes: POST /approvals -> 201 {record} when new, 200 {existing:true, record} when that action_id already exists. ATOMIC create-or-return-existing, so a double submit never produces two prompts or two waits.

nodes.name: Create Verdict
nodes.notes: New -> carry on. Duplicate -> reply already_requested and stop. Store down -> 503 (and an ops alert), never "pending" for a request that does not exist.

nodes.name: Build Slack Prompt
nodes.notes: Slack message with Approve / Deny buttons. Every field is escaped (& < >) so a request cannot inject mentions or links into the approvers' channel. The buttons carry the action_id as their value.

nodes.name: Send Slack Prompt
nodes.notes: Single item, so n8n's own retry works here: up to 3 tries. If it still fails the workflow knows (the original ignored it).

nodes.name: Prompt Result
nodes.notes: Builds the "pending" reply. prompt_delivered tells the caller whether anyone was actually asked.

parameters.jsCode: return [{ json: $input.first().json }];

nodes.name: Join Prompt
nodes.notes: Merges the two Slack branches (sent / not configured) into one path.

nodes.name: Respond Early
nodes.notes: Replies to requests that stop early: bad input (400), bad token (401), misconfigured (500), duplicate (200 already_requested), store down (503).

nodes.name: Respond Pending
nodes.notes: Replies "pending" immediately. Everything after this node (the wait, the auto-decline) happens with no caller attached.

nodes.name: Notify Requester (undelivered)
nodes.notes: Tells the requester their prompt never reached Slack. Skipped silently if NOTIFY_API_URL is blank.

nodes.name: Escalation Planned?
nodes.notes: Only requests whose rule has escalate_after_minutes + escalate_to (and whose own timeout is longer) take the escalation path first.

nodes.name: Wait For Escalation
nodes.notes: Holds until the escalation time. Approvals are recorded in the store, so this node only decides whether to escalate.

nodes.name: Get Approval (escalation)
nodes.notes: GET /approvals/{id}: is it still pending?

nodes.name: Escalation Check
nodes.notes: Still pending at the escalation time? Then prepare the messages for the escalation contacts (via NOTIFY_API_URL) and ops (Slack); the rest of the timeout is waited afterwards. Already decided? Nothing is sent and the wait is skipped.

nodes.name: Any Escalation Notices?
nodes.notes: Slack and/or NOTIFY_API_URL may be blank; then there is nothing to send and the wait simply continues.

parameters.jsCode: return $('Escalation Check').first().json.notices.map((n) => ({ json: n }));

nodes.name: Escalation Notices
nodes.notes: One item per message (one for ops in Slack, one per escalation contact).

nodes.name: Send Escalation Notices
nodes.notes: Sends the escalation messages BEFORE the rest of the wait starts. A failed notice is ignored on purpose (it must not break the approval).

parameters.jsCode: return [{ json: { sent: true } }];

nodes.name: Escalation Sent
nodes.notes: Runs once after all escalation messages went out, then the remaining wait begins.

nodes.name: Wait For Decision
nodes.notes: Holds the execution until the request expires. Waits over about 65 seconds are saved to the n8n database, so they survive a restart. Approvals do NOT resume this node; they are recorded in the store, and this node only auto-declines what is still pending.

nodes.name: Resolve Timeout
nodes.notes: Atomic compare-and-set: only changes the record if it is STILL pending. 200 claimed:true -> we auto-declined it. 409 -> a human already answered: do nothing.

nodes.name: Timeout Verdict
nodes.notes: Claimed -> tell the requester and Slack. Already answered -> nothing. Store error -> alert ops that the request may be stuck pending.

nodes.name: Parse Decision
nodes.notes: Understands both callers: Slack button click (form field `payload`) and direct API {action_id, decision, responder}. Reads the raw bytes for signature checking.

nodes.name: Slack Signature (HMAC)
nodes.notes: Computes HMAC-SHA256 of v0:timestamp:rawbody with your Slack signing secret. Authorize compares it with Slack's X-Slack-Signature header. (A Code node cannot use `crypto` in current n8n.)

nodes.name: Authorize
nodes.notes: Who may decide. Slack: signature must match and be under 5 minutes old. API: x-approver-token header. If you set neither secret the endpoint is OPEN (like the original) and the reply says auth:"open". ALLOWED_APPROVERS limits which people count.

nodes.name: Get Approval
nodes.notes: GET /approvals/{id} -> 200 {record} or 404.

nodes.name: Check Approval
nodes.notes: 404 -> unknown_action. Store error -> 503 retry (never mislabelled as "already_resolved"). Already decided -> already_resolved. Requester approving their own request -> 403 (denying their own is fine). Set SELF_APPROVAL_ALLOWED=true to permit it.

nodes.name: Resolve Approval
nodes.notes: THE decision point. Atomic compare-and-set in the store: with two clicks, or an approval racing the timeout, exactly one call gets claimed:true. With required_approvals above 1 the store records each different approver and only claims on the last one needed (until then: 200 claimed:false pending:true).

nodes.name: Resolve Verdict
nodes.notes: claimed -> approved/denied. Too late (expired) -> 410. Someone else got there first -> already_resolved. Store error -> 503 retry:true, so a failed approval is never reported as "already resolved".

nodes.name: Respond Decision
nodes.notes: The single reply for the decision flow. Replies BEFORE the executor runs, so Slack's 3-second limit is never at risk.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ { action_id: $('Resolve Verdict').first().json.record.action_id, action_type: $('Resolve Verdict').first().json.record.action_type, details: $('Resolve Verdict').first().json.record.details, amount: $('Resolve Verdict').first().json.record.amount, approved_by: $('Authorize').first().json.req.responder, approved_by_all: $('Resolve Verdict').first().json.approved_by_all, idempotency_key: 'approval:' + $('Resolve Verdict').first().json.record.action_id } }}

nodes.name: Execute Action
nodes.notes: POST /execute {action_id, action_type, details, amount, approved_by, approved_by_all, idempotency_key}. The executor gets everything it needs and an idempotency key. NOT retried here: it has side effects, so a retry must be the executor's decision (use the key).

nodes.name: Execution Result
nodes.notes: Success, definite failure (HTTP error) or unknown (no response). Unknown is reported as unknown, never as failed, because the action may have run.

nodes.name: Record Execution
nodes.notes: Writes the outcome back to the store so the record shows what actually happened.

nodes.name: Execution Notices
nodes.notes: Adds an ops alert if the outcome could not be written to the store.

nodes.name: Webhook: Reconcile
nodes.notes: POST /webhook/approvals/reconcile with header x-reconcile-token: runs the reconcile job now and replies with a summary. Off (403) unless CONFIG.RECONCILE_ENABLED is true.

nodes.name: Schedule: Reconcile
nodes.notes: Runs the reconcile job every 15 minutes (edit the interval here). Does nothing unless CONFIG.RECONCILE_ENABLED is true.

parameters.jsCode: return [{ json: { _via: 'schedule' } }];

nodes.name: Mark Reconcile (schedule)
nodes.notes: Tags the run so it takes the reconcile path after CONFIG.

parameters.jsCode: return [{ json: { ...$input.first().json, _via: 'api' } }];

nodes.name: Mark Reconcile (api)
nodes.notes: Tags the run so it takes the reconcile path after CONFIG.

nodes.name: Is Reconcile?
nodes.notes: Requests, decisions and reconcile runs share one CONFIG node and the Approval Policy; this sends reconcile runs down their own path.

nodes.name: Plan Reconcile
nodes.notes: Order: switch (403), reconcile settings (500), token (401, API calls only), CONFIG and policy (500). A scheduled run that cannot run tells ops in Slack.

nodes.name: Reconcile Run
nodes.notes: THE RECONCILE JOB. (1) Auto-declines requests still pending after their deadline. (2) Finds approved requests that never ran: reports them, or (RECONCILE_EXECUTE=true) claims each one atomically and runs it once through the executor with the original idempotency key, then records the outcome. It re-checks everything the store returns, never runs a request with fewer approvals than the policy requires, and never touches requests that failed or have an unknown result (a person decides those).

nodes.name: Webhook Run?
nodes.notes: A reply is only sent to API calls; a scheduled run just goes on to the notices.

nodes.name: Respond Reconcile
nodes.notes: The reply to an API reconcile call: 200 summary, 401, 403 or 500.

nodes.name: Expand Notifications
nodes.notes: Runs AFTER the reply. Turns the notice list into one item per message. Slack text is escaped; Slack or notify are skipped if their URLs are blank.

nodes.name: Send Slack Alert
nodes.notes: Slack-compatible incoming webhook. A failed notice is ignored on purpose: it must not break the decision.

nodes.name: Notify Requester
nodes.notes: POST {NOTIFY_API_URL}/send {to, message}. A failed notice is ignored on purpose.

parameters.content:
## Human Approval Gate
**Setup (about 10 minutes)**
1. Run the backing services (a reference implementation is included: `node 05-human-approval-gate-mock-server.js`, port 4700): approval store, action executor, requester notifications, and a Slack stand-in.
2. Open **CONFIG**: set `APPROVAL_STORE_API_URL`, `ACTION_EXECUTOR_API_URL`, optional `NOTIFY_API_URL` and `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL`.
3. **Lock it down before real use:** set `APPROVER_API_TOKEN` (API approvers send header `x-approver-token`), `SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET` (verifies Slack button clicks), `REQUEST_AUTH_TOKEN` (header `x-request-token`), and `ALLOWED_APPROVERS`. If you set none of them the approve endpoint is OPEN to anyone who can reach it.
4. Activate. Request: `POST /webhook/approvals/request`. Decide: `POST /webhook/approvals/respond` (or Slack buttons).

**Flow:** request -> store record (atomic) -> Slack prompt -> reply "pending" -> wait -> auto-decline if still pending. Decision -> authenticate -> atomic resolve -> reply -> run the action (once) -> record result -> notify.
